questions.q: Which slogan did India’s leaders adopt after 1947?
options: This is not the slogan named.
This is not the slogan named.
questions.rationale: Before 1947, the goal was ‘Quit India’. Then, after 1947, our leaders adopted a new slogan: ‘Build India’.

questions.q: How did Colonel James Irwin describe setting foot on the moon?
options: He did not see it as mere scientific discovery.
An ecstatic experience of feeling oneself in God’s presence
It gave him new spiritual life.
questions.rationale: It was an ecstatic experience he said, to feel oneself in God’s presence, to feel so close to Him that His greatness appeared before one’s eyes.

questions.q: What won the cloth-seller the confidence of his wholesaler?
options: He began with only a few hundred rupees.
This is not in the story.
He always settled his debt before the appointed date.
questions.rationale: This freelance cloth-merchant built up a good deal of trust with his wholesaler, whom he impressed with his honesty and fair dealing.

questions.q: What did Newton write about the rotation of the planets?
options: That there must also be a divine arm in it
Not only the law of gravity.
This is not what he wrote.
He wrote that it is not only due to gravity.
He had just discovered its laws.
questions.rationale: The continuous rotation of the planets is not only due to the law of gravity; there must also be a divine arm in it.

questions.q: To what did the factory owner compare the growth of his business?
options: A tree bearing fruit in a season
A child growing into boyhood over fifteen years
questions.rationale: “Just as a young child grows into boyhood after fifteen years, so does a business. I have not reached this stage in one day.”

questions.article: Moral and Ethical Development in Society
questions.q: What two aspects do all major religions have, according to the article?
options: These are not the two aspects named.
These are not the two aspects named.
Beliefs on one side, the ethical system on the other.
These are not the two aspects named.
questions.rationale: All the major religions have two different aspects to them — theology and the moral scheme.

questions.q: Which personal trait of Mahatma Gandhi does the article begin with?
options: He was a gifted orator from youth
He was very shy by nature
At a London meeting he could not manage his speech.
questions.rationale: Mahatma Gandhi was very shy by nature … it was a long time before he managed to shake off his shyness.

questions.q: What did the porter advise the passenger who had missed his train?
options: To complain to the station master
To wait on the same platform for the next train
Another train would come in a couple of hours.
To go home and return tomorrow
questions.rationale: “There will be another train along in about a couple of hours. Why go away? Just wait here for it on this same platform.”

questions.q: What does the article say of everyone alive today?
options: The article says everyone is in some sense a culprit.
The article says few pay heed.
Everyone will live as long as he wishes
Everyone is to be ‘hanged’ tomorrow, yet is unaware of it
Like a culprit who has heard his sentence, but heedless.
questions.rationale: Everyone alive today is to be ‘hanged’ tomorrow. But everyone is lost in his today and blissfully unaware of his tomorrow.

questions.q: What do the verses quoted (29: 56–59) say every soul shall taste?
options: “and then to Us you shall return.”
questions.rationale: Every soul shall taste death and then to Us you shall return.
